Databasus (Apache-2.0, ~7.4k stars; databasus.com restore-verification docs read 2026-06-15) + pgwatch (BSD-3-Clause, by Cybertec; README read 2026-06-15). METHODOLOGY ONLY, no code bundled, both host-installed/read-only per engagement -> verified-restore-and-baselining.md. Databasus restore-VERIFICATION discipline: a backup that finishes without error is not one you can restore - the only proof is to restore it AND check correctness. Scheduled automated loop: pull latest backup -> restore into a THROWAWAY Docker container of the matching major version (never onto anything live) -> sanity-check restored vs source capturing restore exit code + restored size + schema count + table count + a PER-TABLE ROW-COUNT breakdown -> tear down -> report (alert on failure). The why: checksums catch archive bit-rot only; dump exit codes only prove the command ran; neither catches a missing role grant / missing extension / tablespace mismatch that SILENTLY strips objects - only a real restore that counts rows catches all three. After-backup cadence is the strongest guarantee (cancel stale pending verification when a fresh backup arrives). GFS (grandfather-father-son) retention as independent hourly/daily/weekly/monthly/yearly tiers, auto-pruned, mapped to RPO + legal retention. PITR orchestration: prove a PITR-target restore periodically, not just the latest full, so the WAL chain is proven replayable. Remote/logical mode (no agent, for cloud-managed DBs) vs agent mode (physical + continuous WAL/PITR); verification agent is a separate Go binary on a Docker host you control. pgwatch continuous-baseline-then-tune: collect PG-specific time-series (TPS/latency/cache-hit/locks/replication-lag/bloat-growth/autovacuum/WAL/top-queries via pg_stat_statements) over days-weeks into a Grafana-visualized store, establish the baseline band, tune against the TREND not a snapshot, validate the change on the same series; pgwatch notices drift + picks the moment, postgres_dba diagnoses the culprit (complementary). Gate-0 vs sql-ops-tuning-ha-backup.md: existing had pgBackRest full/diff/incremental + WAL/PITR + checksum/verify + a manual quarterly restore-TEST (bring-up + sanity query) and postgres_dba POINT-IN-TIME diagnostics; net-new = automated throwaway-container restore VERIFICATION with per-table row-count correctness reporting, the checksums-are-insufficient argument, GFS named retention tiers, and continuous longitudinal baselining as the precondition for tuning. No em-dashes.
